name: Peptide eye creams (Eyeliss, Haloxyl)

lead: Eyeliss and Haloxyl are trade names of cosmetic ingredient blends containing short peptides, sold to makers of under-eye creams with claims about reducing puffiness (bags) and dark circles.
The sources available for this entry do not include trial data on these specific blends, so the claims are best understood as manufacturer and marketing positions rather than established results.

paras: Cosmetic peptides are short amino-acid chains. Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, a peptide used in skin creams, is described as derived from an immunoglobulin G sequence and claimed to reduce interleukin-6 and support collagen. Whether such peptides cross the skin in meaningful amounts is discussed in reviews of cosmetic peptides.

Cosmetic-grade peptide creams are sold without prescription. No specific safety data on these blends were found in the sources reviewed; general eyelid-skin irritation from cosmetic ingredients can occur.

lead: Eyeliss and Haloxyl are trade names of peptide-containing cosmetic ingredient complexes used in under-eye creams and marketed for puffiness and dark circles. They are ingredients supplied to cosmetic formulators rather than medicines.

Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, one cosmetic peptide of this kind, is described as a synthetic peptide with a fatty-acid chain to aid skin penetration, claimed to give anti-wrinkle effects and to reduce interleukin-6 production. Its reference literature consists largely of reviews of cosmetic peptides and skin permeability rather than trial results for the peptide alone [1].
Dark circles have several causes, including pigmentation, vascular show-through and thin skin, so a single peptide-based product may not address all presentations [2].

paras: These products are sold in the eye-care category, where peptides are combined with moisturizers and other actives such as caffeine or vitamin C. Caffeine and vitamin C are the topical ingredients general dark-circle references mention; peptides are not discussed there [2].

Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 is grouped with matrikine peptides, reported to promote collagen synthesis and to dampen inflammatory signalling through interleukin-6 [1]. Mechanisms specific to the branded Eyeliss and Haloxyl blends were not available in the sources reviewed.

No studies found. A 2023 clinical study of a multi-peptide anti-aging eye serum is listed in the reference list of the palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 article, but it does not test Eyeliss or Haloxyl specifically [1].
